D.tier: Queued, roster and office levers only

D.t: Debbie Dingell leads by 50.1 in the forecast and wins 100% of simulations. The cushion is about 187,287 votes; a one point swing is about 1,870 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +42.2 and D +57.2. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.

D.h: What the ballots so far say
D.t: The early vote has moved this forecast 0.3 points toward Debbie Dingell. Bank it: chase the remaining mail ballots and low propensity voters who have not voted.

R.t: Heather Smiley trails by 50.1 and wins 0% of simulations. Closing it takes about 93,643 voters switching sides, or 187,287 more net votes from new turnout.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +57.2 and D +42.2. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.

R.h: What the ballots so far say
R.t: The early vote has moved this forecast 0.3 points away from Heather Smiley. Election Day has to make it up: the remaining vote must break harder your way than the forecast expects.
